title: Polymer Microarrays for High Throughput Discovery of Biomaterials
protocol: Weigh out 2 g of poly(hydroxyethyl methacrylate) (pHEMA).
Dissolve pHEMA in 50 mL of 95% ethanol in water.
Sonicate the mixture for typically 24 hours.
Hold an epoxy-functional glass slide with tweezers and dip it into the pHEMA solution, leaving 5 mm uncoated.
Withdraw the slide from the pHEMA solution over a period of 1 second.
Invert the slide and leave it to dry in a near horizontal position for 10 minutes.
Place the pHEMA-coated slide in a slide holder.
Allow the coated slides to remain at atmospheric conditions for one week to evaporate all solvent.
Weigh 120 mg of photoinitiator 2,2-dimethoxy-2-phenyl acetophenone.
Add the photoinitiator to 3 mL of dimethylformamide (DMF).
Mix to form a 4% (w/v) photoinitiator solution.
Add 1 part photoinitiator solution to 3 parts neat monomer in a 384 well source plate.
Pipette 5 μL of photoinitiator solution and 15 μL of monomer into the plate.
Mix solutions thoroughly to achieve a total volume of 20 μL for spot formation.
Clean slotted pins by sonication in dichloromethane for 10 minutes before the print run.
Load clean pins into the pin holder.
Load blotting and array slides.
Fill the chamber with argon to reduce oxygen level to below 2000 ppm.
Maintain humidity at between 30-40% during printing.
Commence the print run.
Load samples from source plate.
Lower pins into solutions at a speed of 25 mm/s, hold for 2.5 seconds, and withdraw at a speed of 25 mm/s.
Blot pins before printing to remove monomer solution from the outside.
Make 10 contacts with a clean glass slide for the first position.
Make 5 contacts for the second position.
Make 4 contacts for the third position.
Make 3 contacts for the fourth position.
Make 2 contacts for each of the next four positions.
Make 1 contact for each of the last three positions.
Ensure each contact lasts 10 ms.
Use an approach and withdrawal speed of 175 mm/s.
Print monomer solutions onto pHEMA coated glass slides.
Make one contact per spot at a pin movement of 175 mm/s.
Maintain a contact time of 10 ms for consistent spot formation.
Ensure an average spot diameter of 400 μm based on viscosity and surface energy.
Typically print three replicate arrays on each glass slide.
Print a total of ten slides in one run, equivalent to 30 spots per cycle.
Wash pins in DMF using a flow bath with agitation.
Use 2.5 L of fresh DMF for the entire wash period.
Irradiate freshly printed slides with short wave UV (365 nm) at 30 mV/cm² during washing.
Irradiate arrays with UV (365 nm) for 10 minutes.
Keep freshly printed arrays at low pressure (<50 mTorr) for 1 week to remove unpolymerized monomer and solvent.
Rotate the array to align with the X-Y movement of the stage.
Locate a corner spot of the array and designate specific coordinates.
Predict the position of each polymer spot using the dimensions of the array.
Dispense a single water drop with a volume of ~400 pL onto each polymer spot using a piezo-driven print head.
Measure the water contact angle (WCA) on an automated Krüss DSA 100 instrument.
Line the X-Y stage with clean Al foil for charge compensation.
Hold the slide in place using metal screw tabs.
Place the sample stage into the transfer chamber of the ToF-SIMS.
Allow the system to pump down until it reaches 1.6 × 10^-6 mbar.
Transfer the sample to the main analysis chamber with a typical vacuum pressure of 1.0 × 10^-8 mbar.
Conduct ToF-SIMS measurements using an ION-ToF IV instrument operated in "bunched mode".
Operate the monoisotopic Bi3+ primary ion source at 25 kV.
Raster a pulsed 1 pA primary ion beam over the analysis area.
Collect both positive and negative secondary ions from a 100 × 100 μm area for a 10-second acquisition time.
Use a high resolution Time-of-Flight analyzer to determine ion masses accurately.
Apply low energy electrons (20 eV) to compensate for surface charging on insulating surfaces.
Place the sample on the large stage AFM with an automated stage.
Home the stage position to the top right corner of the array.
Find the position of the bottom left corner of the array.
Interpolate positions for all other spots based on the corners.
Generate a position list and feed it into the auto-sampling feature of the software.
Enter the sample chamber of a Kratos Axis Ultra XPS instrument and wait until it reaches a pressure below 10-8 Torr.

Select appropriate operation parameters, such as a monochromated x-ray source (Al, 1486.6 eV), anode potential and current (10kV and 15mA), aperture size (110μm), pass energy (80 eV for wide scan and 20 eV for high resolution scan).
Focus the X-ray source using two opposite corners of the microarray and optimize the oxygen signal from the sample.
Determine the x and y positions of individual spots and log them as a position list.
Write a program chart for data acquisition, including wide scans and high resolution scans for specific elements.
Calibrate the Raman signal using a silicon wafer at the Raman shift of Si at 520.7 cm-1.
Place the sample on the stage and adjust the focus of the laser (wavelength = 523 nm) to maximize the C-H Raman shift at 2950 cm-1.
Set the position of the centre of the top left spot on the microarray as the origin.
Setup a map of the microarray using the array function on the LabRAM HR software.
Acquire 10 spectra cumulatively for each sample with an irradiation time of 0.5 s.
Cultivate a bacterial strain overnight at 37 °C in 10 mL of LB media in a 50 mL falcon tube with shaking at 200 rpm.
Measure the OD600 of the bacterial culture.
Inoculate sufficient overnight culture into 15 mL RPMI-1640 defined media to achieve a final OD600 of 0.01.
Prewash arrays in sterilized distilled water for 10 minutes.
Place prewashed array slides in a clean petri dish.
UV sterilize the array slides for 10 minutes.
Place a slide with the array into a petri dish and add 15 mL of inoculated RPMI-1640 media.
Incubate another slide with non-inoculated RPMI-1640 as a control in a separate petri dish.
Incubate both slides at 37 °C for 72 hours with shaking at 60 rpm.
Wash the slides twice with 15 mL of sterile PBS.
Wash the slides twice with 15 mL of sterile distilled water.
Air-dry the slides.
Image the slides using a GenePix Autoloader 4200AL Scanner with a 488 nm excitation laser and standard blue emission filter.
Include appropriate positive controls for bacterial response normalization.
Acquire total fluorescence intensity from polymer spots using GenePix Pro 6 software.
Subtract fluorescence measured on media control from the slide incubated with bacteria to find bacterial growth fluorescence.
Stain slides with 20 μM SYTO17 nucleic acid dye at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Image stained slides using a Carl Zeiss LSM 700 Laser Scanning Microscope with ZEN 2009 imaging software.
Determine coverage of bacteria on the surface using Image J software.
